input.quote: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: This is a 24-month post-term, all-territory, undefined-scope non-compete binding us — squarely walk-away under the playbook, and it also contradicts Section 12.3, which states we have made no non-compete commitment. We have deleted it and can offer the narrowed fallback (named competing product, term only) if Vendor needs protection.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds us; Section 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to engage any supplier. The only related burdens (the match-offer clause in Section 7.2 and the take-or-pay in Section 2.1) are addressed under the MFN and MINCOMMIT rules rather than flagged twice here.

input.quote: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 is an open-ended MFN/right-of-first-refusal running against us: we would have to disclose and match any better third-party offer, with no product limit, time limit or comparison carve-outs. That is the walk-away case, and it conflicts with Section 12.3, so we have deleted it; MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.

input.quote: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: This is a one-sided 24-month no-hire covering every Vendor employee and expressly overriding any general-advertising or unsolicited-application carve-out — walk-away territory. We have narrowed it to the fallback: mutual, personnel involved in the Services, 12 months, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
